cards.text: Friend, John is telling what God showed him in a vision (Revelation 1:1). He keeps watching. He sees an angel coming down from heaven with a key, holding a great chain in his hand.

cards.question: The angel coming down from heaven holds the key to the ___.

cards.text: And that great chain is not for decoration, friend. The angel is about to use it on somebody.

cards.question: Who does the angel seize with that great chain?

cards.text: That dragon is the ancient serpent, the devil and Satan. FOUR names, friend, and I've only got two, one of them carved on my handle.

cards.question: The angel binds the dragon for ___ years.

cards.text: The angel throws him into the Abyss, shuts it and seals it over him. I spent years shut in a junk drawer, friend, but at least mine popped open every time somebody needed TAPE.

cards.question: Why is the Abyss shut and sealed over the dragon?

answers.text: So he cannot deceive the nations
So he cannot reach the heavens
So he cannot harm the angels

cards.question: Once the thousand years are complete, the dragon stays sealed in the Abyss for good.

cards.text: Then John sees thrones, and those seated on them have been given authority to judge. He also sees the souls of people who had been beheaded.

cards.question: Why had the people John sees been beheaded?

answers.text: For their service in the temple
For their defense of the city

cards.question: Along with those souls, John sees people who had not worshiped the beast or received its mark.
What happens to those souls and to the ones who refused the beast?

answers.text: They come to life and reign with Christ
They rest under the altar a while longer
They stand guard over the sealed Abyss

cards.text: And the rest of the dead? John says they don't come back to life until the thousand years are complete.

cards.question: John says this coming to life is the first ___.

cards.text: Then John says, "Blessed and holy are those who share in the first resurrection!" Blessed AND holy, friend, that's a double batch.

cards.question: The second death has power over those who share in the first resurrection.
What will those who share in the first resurrection be as they reign with Christ?

answers.text: Priests of God and of Christ
Guards at the gates of the city

cards.text: When the thousand years are complete, Satan is released from his prison. A THOUSAND years, friend, and he walks straight out to deceive the nations in the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog.

cards.question: Satan deceives the nations of Gog and Magog. What is he gathering them for?
John says the number of that gathered army is like the ___ of the seashore.

cards.text: That army marches across the broad expanse of the earth and surrounds the camp of the saints and the beloved city. And I used to think a junk drawer full of rubber bands was crowded.

cards.question: The camp of the saints and the beloved city are surrounded. Then what happens?

answers.text: Fire comes down from heaven and consumes them
The saints march out and drive them away
The army turns around and runs back home

cards.text: Then the devil, the one who deceived them, is thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur. A thousand years locked up, friend, and the big comeback lasts about THREE verses.

cards.question: When the devil is thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur, he's the first one in there.
John says the devil, the beast and the false prophet will be tormented there for a thousand years and then it ends.

cards.text: Then John sees a great white throne and the One seated on it. And something flees from His presence.

cards.question: What flees from the presence of the One seated on the great white throne?

cards.text: John sees the dead, great and small, standing before the throne, and books are opened. Great AND small, friend. Nobody sleeps through this one.

cards.question: One of the books opened before the throne has a name: the Book of ___.
How are the dead judged before the great white throne?

answers.text: By their deeds recorded in the books
By the gifts they bring to the throne
By the land they were born in

cards.text: And nobody gets missed, friend. The sea gives up its dead.

cards.question: The sea gives up its dead, and ___ and ___ give up their dead too.

cards.text: Then Death and Hades themselves are thrown into the lake of fire. After years in a junk drawer waiting to get tossed out, I never thought I'd CHEER for something getting thrown away.

cards.question: John calls the lake of fire the second death.
At the great white throne, who is thrown into the lake of fire?

answers.text: Anyone not written in the Book of Life
Anyone who rose up out of the sea
Anyone who stood before the throne

findings.problem: Most of the early choice cards in stop 1 can only be answered by luck. Card 2 asks for the Abyss, card 4 asks the dragon versus the beast versus the false prophet, and card 6 asks for a thousand years. The story cards before them (cards 1, 3 and 5) give nothing to reason from. Card 3 gives no hint at all about who will be seized, and none of the three answer figures has been introduced. That is three of the first four choice cards as pure discovery, which is more than 'a few'.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: This story card cites Revelation 20:2 but tells nothing from the verse. It only says the chain is about to be used on somebody, so it is filler. Its line ('not for decoration') is a mild, pleasant-dad line, not a real laugh.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The beast shows up here for the first time in the walkthrough, apart from a wrong answer on card 4. It is never said who the beast is. Stop 2 card 8 then names the beast and the false prophet together, again without saying who either one is. They never appear on a story card at all, so the only place the baker learns they were already in the lake of fire (20:10) is inside a true or false statement.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: 'The ones who refused the beast' adds an active refusal that the text doesn't state. Revelation 20:4 says they 'had not worshiped the beast or its image and had not received its mark.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: 'This coming to life' points back to cards the baker can no longer see. The card just before it (card 14) is about the rest of the dead, who come back to life after the thousand years. So the question can read as calling their later coming to life the first resurrection.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'He walks straight out' adds immediacy that the text doesn't give. Revelation 20:7-8 says only that he 'will be released' and 'will go out to deceive the nations.'

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'shells' is not a real detail from the Bible. This is a 'which thing' question, so its wrong answers need to be real Bible details.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The question names only the camp of the saints and the beloved city, and the army is never mentioned. That makes the right answer 'Fire comes down from heaven and consumes them' read as though the fire consumes the saints and the city. Revelation 20:9 shows the fire consumes the army that surrounded them.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: 'And nobody gets missed' is presented as a storyteller line, but it states a claim of fact that every person is accounted for. Revelation 20:13 says only that the sea, Death and Hades gave up their dead.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.
